evidence: Integration with WhatsApp and Whatsmeow is cleanly decoupled via adapter packages (pkg/whatsmeow, pkg/whatsapp).
The App struct is the universal junction for all collaborator handoffs, creating a single, rigid point of integration for the entire codebase.
Lifecycles and context are explicitly passed through layer boundaries, ensuring proper timeout and cancellation propagation.
Orchestration of complex flows (e.g., in chatbot_processor.go) happens as a monolithic block of logic rather than a composition of clean-room collaborators.

strengths: Effective use of the Adapter pattern to isolate third-party provider volatility.
Strong and consistent propagation of context.Context throughout the stack.
Clear entry/exit points for data translation between handlers and adapters.
mid_level_elegance.issue_character: Integration mechanics are robust at the edges but monolithic and overly coupled in the core.
mid_level_elegance.score_rationale: Score 65.0 because the handoffs to external systems are elegant and well-protected. However, internal handoffs between domain modules are poor because the monolithic handler structure and 'god object' App struct stifle the opportunity for true compositional architecture.

issues.summary: Integration flows are implemented as monolithic blocks instead of collaborator compositions
evidence: Complex multi-step processes are coded as sequential logic within a single receiver method.
issues.suggestion: Refactor complex domain flows into orchestrator services that compose smaller, specialized collaborators.

issues.summary: All internal handoffs are forced through the monolithic App struct
evidence: Every collaborator (DB, Redis, Logger, WhatsApp client) is tied to the App struct, making it impossible to separate concerns at the integration layer.
issues.suggestion: Introduce smaller, interface-based dependency bundles for specific domain subsystems.

root_causes: Prioritization of easy access to dependencies (global App) over strict interface segregation.
likely_symptoms: Difficulty mocking specific collaborators for integration tests, wide blast area when changing any part of the App configuration.
